ai.description: This frog reaches 25–30 mm. It is brown with a distinct cream-colored snout tip and granular skin. It is characterized by prominent, rounded toe pads and a lack of webbing on the feet.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Nyctibatrachus kempholeyensis* is best distinguished by its distinctively pointed, elongated snout and the presence of prominent, fleshy webbing extending to the toe tips.
ai.habitat: The Kempholey night frog inhabits the evergreen forests of the central Western Ghats, typically found near rocky streams at elevations between 600 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Kempholey Night Frog is strictly nocturnal, spending its nights foraging for small invertebrates along the mossy, spray-drenched rocks of cascading forest streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Nyctibatrachus kempholeyensis* breeds during the monsoon, laying clutches of 15–25 eggs in rock crevices or on vegetation near streams, where males provide parental care.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Kempholey Night Frog is endemic to the central Western Ghats in Karnataka, India, typically inhabiting streams at elevations between 800 and 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Kempholey Night Frog emits a series of high-pitched, insect-like chirps while perched on rocks or vegetation near fast-flowing streams in the Western Ghats.
